newsitem.title: USA: SYSCO comfortable with Q2 estimates - CEO.
newsitem.headline: SYSCO comfortable with Q2 estimates - CEO.

text.p: SYSCO Corp president and chief executive officer Bill Lindig said Friday he was comfortable with estimates the food service giant would earn $0.42 to $0.44 in the second quarter of fiscal 1997.
Lindig also said SYSCO's board of directors had voted to raise the quarterly dividend to $0.15 from $0.13.
"I think we're comfortable with a(n estimates) range of $0.42 to $0.44" for the second quarter, he told Reuters at the company's annual meeting.
SYSCO earned $0.41 a share in the fiscal first quarter, which ended Sept. 28.

Lindig said the new quarterly dividend of $0.15 a share was 15 percent higher than the previous rate and maintained SYSCO's record of hiking its dividend every year since it went public in March 1970.
He also that capital expenditures for fiscal 1997 would be around $250 million, up from $236 million in 1996.
Houston-based SYSCO, which had revenues of $13.4 billion in fiscal 1996, is the United States' largest food service distribution and marketing company.
